## Warm-up retrieval

::: {.mcq data-correct="c"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q1. Which component of the grammar of graphics is responsible for telling `ggplot2` *what kind* of mark to draw (points, bars, lines)?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>data</li>
  <li>aesthetic mapping (`aes`)</li>
  <li>geometric object (`geom`)</li>
  <li>facet</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(c)</strong> `geom_*()` functions specify the visual mark; `aes()` is the mapping between data and visual properties; `data` is the data frame.</div>
:::

## Check-in: The pipe operator: `|>`

Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q1. Which `dplyr` verb keeps only the rows where `carrier == &quot;DL&quot;`?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>`select()`</li>
  <li>`filter()`</li>
  <li>`arrange()`</li>
  <li>`mutate()`</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> `filter()` keeps rows matching a logical condition. `select()` picks columns; `arrange()` sorts rows; `mutate()` creates new columns.</div>
:::

## Check-in: `summarize` variables

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q3. Why do many `summarize()` calls include `na.rm = TRUE`?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>To increase the precision of the result</li>
  <li>To exclude missing (`NA`) values from the calculation</li>
  <li>To remove negative values</li>
  <li>To round to whole numbers</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> `na.rm = TRUE` tells the summary function to skip `NA` values. Without it, *any* missing value will cause the entire summary to return `NA`. (But always think about *why* the values are missing before reaching for it.)</div>
:::

## Check-in: `group_by` rows

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q4. What's the difference between `filter(flights, carrier == &quot;DL&quot;)` and `filter(flights, carrier = &quot;DL&quot;)`?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>They're equivalent</li>
  <li>The second uses `=` and triggers an error inside `filter()` — `==` is the *comparison* operator; `=` is for naming function arguments</li>
  <li>The first returns Delta flights; the second returns all flights</li>
  <li>Both work but the second is slower</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> `==` compares; `=` assigns argument values. Mixing them up is one of the most common dplyr errors.</div>
:::

## Check-in: `mutate` existing variables

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q5. After running `flights |> mutate(gain = arr_delay - dep_delay)` *without* `<-`, the `flights` data frame:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Has the new `gain` column added</li>
  <li>Is unchanged — the result was computed but not stored anywhere</li>
  <li>Has the new column AND its previous columns are removed</li>
  <li>Errors</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> Verbs like `mutate()` *return* a modified copy. To keep it, you must reassign with `<-`: `flights <- flights |> mutate(...)`. Without that, the modified version is printed and discarded.</div>
:::

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q6. `flights |> arrange(dep_delay)` returns rows sorted by departure delay. The first row is most likely:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>The flight with the largest delay</li>
  <li>The flight with the most negative `dep_delay` (i.e., it left earliest before its scheduled time)</li>
  <li>A flight with no delay</li>
  <li>A random flight</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> `arrange()` sorts ascending by default. The smallest value (most negative) comes first. Use `arrange(desc(dep_delay))` for largest first.</div>
:::

## Check-in: `join` data frames

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="a"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q7. `flights |> inner_join(airlines, by = &quot;carrier&quot;)` returns:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Only rows from `flights` whose `carrier` value also appears in `airlines`</li>
  <li>All rows from `flights`, with airline info filled in where matched (`NA` otherwise)</li>
  <li>All rows from `airlines`, with flight info added</li>
  <li>The union of both data frames</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(a)</strong> **Inner** join keeps only rows matched in BOTH tables. (b) describes a `left_join`; (c) is a `right_join`. With `nycflights23`, every carrier in `flights` is in `airlines`, so the visible row count is the same — but the conceptual difference matters when keys don't all match.</div>
:::

## Check-in: Other verbs

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q8. `flights |> filter(dep_delay > 60 | arr_delay > 60)` returns rows where:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>BOTH `dep_delay` and `arr_delay` exceed 60</li>
  <li>EITHER `dep_delay` or `arr_delay` (or both) exceeds 60</li>
  <li>Neither delay exceeds 60</li>
  <li>An error</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> `|` is the *OR* operator in R. `&` is *AND*. Confusing the two is a common student error.</div>
:::
